title: Cancellation of a quasicategorical equivalence
statement: Use quasicategories, simplicial functors and coherent natural equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Joyal model structure and its quasicategory characterization from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] and [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations]. Let $X,Y$ be quasicategories and let $f:X\to Y$, $r:Y\to X$ be simplicial functors. If $f$ is a categorical equivalence and there is a coherent natural equivalence $rf\simeq1_X$, then $r$ is a categorical equivalence. Consequently $r$ admits a coherent quasi-inverse and is fully faithful and essentially surjective.

source.place: The cancellation subargument in the simplex-relative inverse proof: $rf\simeq1_X$, two-out-of-three with $f$, and the Joyal characterization of the resulting equivalence.

proof.text: Put $u=rf:X\to X$, and let $\eta:u\simeq1_X$ be the given equivalence edge. The identity $1_X$ is a simplicial quasi-inverse to $u$: both $1_Xu$ and $u1_X$ equal $u$, so the same edge $\eta$ provides both required coherent natural equivalences with $1_X$. This is precisely the functor-equivalence data of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; it requires no triangle identity relating the two comparisons. Apply clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] with both categories equal to $X$. It makes $u=rf$ a Joyal weak equivalence, equivalently a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent realization foundations: agent expansion of the cancellation subargument, first establishing that the composite is a categorical equivalence.

proof.text: In the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], categorical equivalences are the weak equivalences and obey two-out-of-three. Apply this to the composable simplicial maps $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{r}X$. The first map is a categorical equivalence by hypothesis and their composite $rf$ is one by step 1; therefore $r$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent realization foundations: two-out-of-three cancellation for the map constructed in the simplex-relative inverse argument.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] to $r:Y\to X$. Both $Y$ and $X$ are quasicategories in the chosen universe. It supplies a simplicial functor $s:X\to Y$ with coherent natural equivalences $sr\simeq1_Y$ and $rs\simeq1_X$. Thus $r$ is a functor equivalence in the stipulated sense. The assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] that every functor equivalence induces equivalences on all mapping spaces gives, for every $y,y'\in Y$, a weak homotopy equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_Y(y,y')\to\operatorname{Map}_X(r(y),r(y'))$. This is exactly full faithfulness under [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent realization foundations: consequences of the cancelled equivalence for mapping spaces and coherent quasi-inverses.

proof.text: For each vertex $x\in X$, take $s(x)\in Y$. Evaluation at $x$ sends the coherent natural equivalence $rs\simeq1_X$ of step 3 to an equivalence edge $r(s(x))\simeq x$ in $X$: evaluation is restriction along $\{x\}\hookrightarrow X$, and it sends the inverse edge and its two inverse triangles to an inverse edge and two inverse triangles. These are exactly the equivalence witnesses of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence every vertex of $X$ is equivalent to an object in the image of $r$, which is essential surjectivity.

source.place: Lecture II, basic facts (1) and (3), printed p.14: evaluation of an equivalence edge and its inverse triangles; the essential-image inference is elementary.

split_report.summary: Proved cancellation with four steps and no new nodes: the given comparison makes rf a functor equivalence with identity quasi-inverse; the existing Joyal dictionary makes rf weak, and the model two-out-of-three gives r weak. The same dictionary supplies a coherent quasi-inverse, existing functor calculus gives full faithfulness, and evaluation of inverse triangles gives essential surjectivity. Retained the statement and inherited searches, appended actual logged Mathlib searches, and removed the functor-calculus theorem from statement dependencies because it is used only in the proof.

tool_uses.why: Only its general theorem that every functor equivalence induces equivalences on mapping spaces is used to obtain full faithfulness. It is a generic quasicategory tool; the item unit supplies no mapping-space consequence of equivalence.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q85-9bcad331e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and the sources it cites. Shape: one commit with the item node and the report, no new nodes, and the statement is byte-identical to the unsplit base (compared with the side DAG copy). The one stmt_deps change drops lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus, which the statement does not use; it stays in proof_deps, and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. Step 1 is correct: with u=rf, the identity is a simplicial quasi-inverse. The composites 1_X u and u 1_X are both literally u, so the given edge u≃1_X supplies both coherent equivalences that def-cbc requires (no triangle identity). Clause (2) of lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations, applied with both categories equal to X, then makes rf a Joyal weak equivalence, which that clause identifies with a categorical equivalence. Step 2 is correct: lem-coef-joyal-model-structure literally states that the weak equivalences are the categorical equivalences and satisfy two-out-of-three; applied to X→Y→X with f and rf weak, r is weak. Step 3 is correct: clause (2) applied to r gives s with sr≃1_Y and rs≃1_X. The cone-calculus sentence 'Every functor equivalence induces equivalences on all mapping spaces' is exactly def-cbc's full faithfulness, since spaces are taken up to weak homotopy equivalence. Step 4 is genuinely elementary: evaluation at x is the simplicial restriction along {x}×Δ^n, which carries an equivalence edge and its two inverse 2-simplices to an equivalence edge r(s(x))≃x. I checked this against Scholze, Lecture II, printed pp.14-15, basic facts (1) and (3). Accepted tool_use: lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus, used only for its mapping-space clause. Its unit sk-prop-sf-cbc is not reachable from sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, no node of that unit gives this fact, and 263 nodes of the unit already record it as a tool. Small cases: X empty forces Y empty, so the statement is vacuously true; on nerves it reduces to ordinary cancellation; and the hypothesis on f is needed (a point into a discrete two-point set with the collapse map has rf=id but r is not fully faithful). Duplicate candidates read: lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image, lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-functor-equivalence-lift, lem-coef-joyal-small-test-universe-invariance and lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve; none states this cancellation. Cycle check: the dependency closures of the four cited nodes (3, 68, 75 and 142 nodes) contain neither the item nor its parent lem-coef-cartesian-simplex-inverse-extension. The parent's step 10 uses the statement exactly as written. Minor point, not a fault of this delivery: the imported phrase 'essentially surjective' has no definition node, but step 4 states the meaning. HTT is not archived, so I relied on the archived DAG statements instead. No SGA source is used. No fixes were written.
